note: Initial rule list. The PI will replace this file with the final version; the site reads only the fields below. label: the label the rule supports (normal / anomaly / unknown). note_required: a note must be written when this rule is chosen.

rules.label: anomaly
rules.title: TLB error interrupt
rules.text: KERNEL FATAL “… TLB error interrupt” (published category KERNDTLB).

rules.label: anomaly
rules.title: Data storage interrupt
rules.text: KERNEL FATAL “data storage interrupt” (KERNSTOR).

rules.label: anomaly
rules.title: ciod: error reading message prefix after LOAD_MESSAGE
rules.text: APP FATAL “ciod: Error reading message prefix after LOAD_MESSAGE on CioStream socket to …” (APPSEV).

rules.label: anomaly
rules.title: Lustre mount FAILED
rules.text: KERNEL FATAL “Lustre mount FAILED : … ” (KERNMNTF).

rules.label: anomaly
rules.title: rts: kernel terminated
rules.text: KERNEL FATAL “rts: kernel terminated for reason …” (KERNTERM).

rules.label: anomaly
rules.title: Error receiving packet on tree network
rules.text: KERNEL FATAL “Error receiving packet on tree network, expecting type … instead of type …” (KERNREC).

rules.label: anomaly
rules.title: ciod: failed to read message prefix on control stream
rules.text: APP FATAL “ciod: failed to read message prefix on control stream …” (APPREAD).

rules.label: anomaly
rules.title: rts panic
rules.text: KERNEL FATAL “rts panic! - stopping execution” (KERNRTSP).

rules.label: anomaly
rules.title: ciod: error reading message prefix (other message types)
rules.text: APP FATAL “ciod: Error reading message prefix after <message type> on CioStream socket …” for message types other than LOAD_MESSAGE (APPSEV).

rules.label: anomaly
rules.title: ciod: node map — No child processes
rules.text: APP FATAL “ciod: Error creating node map from file … No child processes” (APPCHILD). Only the reason “No child processes” is an alert; other reasons (Permission denied, Bad address, …) are not.

rules.label: anomaly
rules.title: Machine check interrupt
rules.text: KERNEL FATAL “machine check interrupt …” (KERNMC).

rules.label: anomaly
rules.title: Kernel panic
rules.text: KERNEL FATAL “kernel panic” (KERNPAN).

rules.label: anomaly
rules.title: Other published BGL alert category
rules.text: Matches another alert category from the published BGL alert list. Name the category and quote the key text in the note.

rules.label: normal
rules.title: Non-alert severity level
rules.text: Level is INFO, WARNING, SEVERE, ERROR (anything other than FATAL / FAILURE). All published BGL alerts come from FATAL / FAILURE levels, so such lines are normal even if they contain words like “error”.

rules.label: normal
rules.title: FATAL / FAILURE but no alert rule matches
rules.text: The level is FATAL or FAILURE but the message matches none of the published alert rules. Explain in the note why you consider it routine.

rules.label: anomaly
rules.title: VAPI: EVAPI_process_local_mad failed
rules.text: kernel “[KERNEL_IB][…] … EVAPI_process_local_mad failed, return code = … (Fatal error (Local Catastrophic Error))” (VAPI).

rules.label: anomaly
rules.title: PBS_CON: connection refused
rules.text: pbs_mom “Connection refused (111) in open_demux …” (PBS_CON).

rules.label: anomaly
rules.title: MPT: SCSI task abort
rules.text: kernel “mptscsih: ioc0: attempting task abort! …” (MPT).

rules.label: anomaly
rules.title: EXT_FS: ext3 error
rules.text: kernel “EXT3-fs error (device …): … ” (EXT_FS).

rules.label: anomaly
rules.title: CPU: losing ticks
rules.text: kernel “Losing some ticks… checking if CPU frequency changed.” (CPU).

rules.label: anomaly
rules.title: SCSI: rejecting I/O to offline device
rules.text: kernel “scsi…: rejecting I/O to offline device” (SCSI).

rules.label: anomaly
rules.title: ECC: memory error
rules.text: Server Administrator memory-device ECC error report (ECC).

rules.label: anomaly
rules.title: PBS_BFD: bad file descriptor
rules.text: pbs_mom “Bad file descriptor (9) in tm_request …” (PBS_BFD).

rules.label: anomaly
rules.title: CHK_DSK: disk fault
rules.text: check-disks “… Fault Status assert …” (CHK_DSK).

rules.label: anomaly
rules.title: NMI received
rules.text: kernel “Uhhuh. NMI received …” (NMI).

rules.label: normal
rules.title: Routine operation (no alert rule matches)
rules.text: Matches none of the published alert rules and records the normal result of a routine operation. Say what the operation is in the note (e.g. “routine service start/stop”).

rules.label: normal
rules.title: Complete normal lifecycle
rules.text: Only allocation, write (3 replicas), read / verify and delete events; replica counts are consistent and deletion is complete. A different event order does not matter. “Got exception while serving” during the read phase is part of normal reads.

rules.label: normal
rules.title: Normal lifecycle without deletion
rules.text: Complete, consistent write (and possibly read / verify) of all replicas; the block was simply never deleted within the log.

rules.label: normal
rules.title: Normal re-replication
rules.text: Extra replica transfer (ask … to replicate, Starting thread to transfer, Transmitted block) that completes consistently.

rules.label: anomaly
rules.title: Write / receive exception
rules.text: Exceptions on the write path: writeBlock … received exception, PacketResponder … Exception / Interrupted, Exception in receiveBlock, Exception writing block to mirror, Receiving empty packet.

rules.label: anomaly
rules.title: Inconsistent replica bookkeeping
rules.text: Redundant addStoredBlock, addStoredBlock for a block that does not belong to any file, replica counts that do not match, or a block removed from neededReplications.

rules.label: anomaly
rules.title: Delete / transfer failure
rules.text: Unexpected error trying to delete block (BlockInfo not found), Failed to transfer, PendingReplicationMonitor timed out, block is not valid / cannot be written to.

rules.label: unknown
rules.title: Cannot decide
rules.text: The rules and the visible evidence do not settle the label. Describe what is missing in the note.

rules.title: Other reason
rules.text: None of the listed rules applies. Explain your reasoning in the note.
